occupants.note: A STATED USE, NOT AN OCCUPANT (data/reconstruction/1835_stated_uses.json, T-1988; liberty L310). No household holds this roof and nobody is named for it: what is stated is what the building was for. The A1 line of the family crosswalk (a stable with a hay loft) and the West recipe's own cluster, w2_canal_randolph_teamster: loose mixed lots south and west of the documented Western Hotel's teamster yard. T-1781 redealt this slot from a W4 workshop to an A1 stable (the placement policy refuses a workshop on a light street, and the slot and its position stand), and the recipe gives it no `yard_group`. No seated dwelling is tied to it: the nearest, recon_1835_blk_randolph_clinton_d3_04, is 46.0 m away on another block, and nothing committed joins the two. So the row states the use and serves nobody. A stable on the approach keeps horses; nobody sleeps in it. The roof's own existence, position and footprint remain the invention they were.
